requirements.evidence: Entities migration has id/name/slug unique `entities_slug_unique`/timestamps/softDeletes (database/migrations/2026_10_29_035213_create_entities_table.php:11-19); memberships migration has cascading FKs, `role` default 'employee', unique `(entity_id, user_id)` and `owner_seq` generated column + `entity_memberships_one_owner` unique (database/migrations/2026_10_29_035214_create_entity_memberships_table.php:15-23). Contract fully present: Entity (app/Models/Entity.php:16-49 incl. getRouteKeyName/SoftDeletes/memberships/users/owner), EntityMembership (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:12-68 scopes, cast, relations), UserRole::manageable() = [Admin, Employee] (app/Models/UserRole.php:16-19), User relations/membershipFor (app/Models/User.php:38-56), factories (database/factories/EntityFactory.php, EntityMembershipFactory.php with owner/admin/employee states), and all policy methods asked for (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:11-39, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:11-45).

conventions.evidence: Policies used for authorization, deliberate `$fillable` (app/Models/Entity.php:18, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:15), reversible migrations with generated-style docblocks (all migrations have `down()`), and docs/CHANGELOG kept in sync (CHANGELOG.md:9, docs/database-schema.md:151-152). Deviation: no tests ship with the production code, violating the TDD convention; `User::membershipFor()` (app/Models/User.php:53) also lacks the PHPDoc the other touched methods have, and docs/database-schema.md:151 inaccurately says `Entity::owner()` "scopes `memberships()`" when it is a `hasOne(...)->where(...)`.

security.evidence: Authorization is entirely server-side in policies (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:11-39, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:11-45), policies are the correct zero-argument, auto-discovered classes, `$fillable` excludes the generated `owner_seq` (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:15) so mass assignment is controlled, and there is no Blade/output in the change. Gap: `assignRole` (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:16-25) only verifies the actor is owner/admin, so an admin may target the owner's membership and demote the owner, leaving zero owners.

tests.evidence: change.diff contains no test files at all: it ends with docs/database-schema.md (change.diff:486-556) after the migrations/factories, and no tests/ or *Test.php file is added anywhere in the 556-line diff. Nothing covers the generated-column single-owner constraint, cascade deletes, factory states or any policy allow/deny path.

simplicity.evidence: Small focused classes that reuse `membershipFor()` instead of duplicating queries (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:21-39) and delegate `delete` to `update` (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:32-35); `owner()` uses a simple `hasOne` scope (app/Models/Entity.php:46-49). Minor excess: `roleOf()` (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:46-51) is dead defensive code because the `role` cast (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:21-25) already guarantees a `UserRole`, and the same actor-role lookup is repeated in four policy methods.

readability.evidence: Clear names (`membershipFor`, `manageSettings`, `scopeOwner`), small single-purpose methods, consistent PHPDoc generics (`@return HasMany<EntityMembership>`, `Builder<EntityMembership>`), no debug output or dead code; style matches the existing User model (app/Models/User.php:31-56).

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: two migrations, three models + enum, two factories, two policies, User relations, docs/database-schema.md and the CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md:9); no routes, Livewire components, session handling or other out-of-scope features were added.

issues.explanation: The change ships migrations, models, factories and policies with zero Pest/PHPUnit tests, violating the project's "no production code without a test" rule and leaving the DB single-owner constraint, cascades and every policy decision unverified.

`assignRole` only checks that the actor is owner/admin, so an admin can act on the owner's membership and demote the owner, leaving the entity with no owner (deletion of the owner membership is protected, but its role is not).

The doc claims `Entity::owner()` "scopes `memberships()` to `role = owner`", but app/Models/Entity.php:46-49 implements it as `hasOne(EntityMembership::class)->where(...)`; the docs no longer describe the code.
The new public `membershipFor()` method has no PHPDoc, unlike the other public methods touched in this change.
`roleOf()` is redundant defensive code: the `role` cast already returns a `UserRole`, so the `tryFrom((string) $role)` fallback can never be needed.

review.summary: The change implements the full entity/membership persistence layer, models, enum, factories and both policies, and updates the schema docs and changelog, meeting the task contract. It ships without any tests, which violates the project's mandatory TDD convention and is the blocking issue; there is also a limited authorization gap where an admin can demote the owner.
